name: Air Fryer Greek Tzatziki Fish Tacos

components.name: Crispy Fish Strips

ingredients.name: Raw boneless cod or firm white fish, cut into taco strips
Raw whole egg, beaten, without shell

steps: Pat fish strips dry. Set flour, beaten eggs and panko in separate bowls. Coat strips lightly in flour, then egg, then panko; discard any coating left in contact with raw fish.
Spray the air-fryer basket. Air fry breaded fish at 195 C for 8-12 minutes, turning once until crisp and internal temperature reaches 63 C. Cook batches without stacking.
Assemble two fish tacos per serving with measured tzatziki and raw vegetables; alternatively pack fish apart from tortillas and sauce for meal prep.
Reheat fish in the air fryer; add the cold tzatziki, tomato and lettuce only at serving time to avoid sogginess.

components.name: Flour Tortillas

ingredients.name: Eight soft flour tortillas, 40 g each

steps: Briefly warm the tortillas, chop lettuce and tomatoes, and portion toppings.

components.name: Tzatziki & Salad

ingredients.name: Raw cucumber, grated and squeezed dry

steps: Mix Greek yogurt, finely squeezed cucumber, garlic, lemon and dill into tzatziki. Refrigerate while preparing the fish.

notes: Draft — needs Mirna review: not kitchen-tested yet; macros and cooked yields are estimates.
Skinnytaste Greek fish taco concept and air-fryer technique; quantities scaled for four complete meals.
Planning: SECONDARY appliance for warming tortillas optional.
Freezer: breaded fish can freeze, but loses some crispness; tortillas freeze separately; tzatziki and salad NOT freezer-friendly
Dietary: Fish, egg, wheat, milk; fresh cucumber in tzatziki.

Refrigerate within 2 hours (1 hour above 32°C) in shallow containers at 4°C or colder, for 3–4 days at most, and follow the shorter seafood limit above. Cook fish and shellfish to 63°C and reheat leftovers to at least 74°C.

preservationAndReheating: Refrigerate cooked food promptly in shallow covered containers. Target within 2 hours, or 1 hour when ambient temperature exceeds 32 C.
Refrigerate at 4 C or below for 3-4 days maximum; for many fish and shrimp dishes, prioritize eating within 1-2 days for quality and freeze later-week cooked portions promptly.

Cook fish and crustaceans to 63 C (145 F) or applicable local food-safety standard, and reheat cooked leftovers to 74 C. For crab cakes containing egg binder and purchased cooked crab, reheat to 74 C.
When recipe includes rice, cool rapidly and refrigerate promptly; do not leave cooked rice at room temperature.
Freeze in suitable airtight food-safe containers. Defrost in refrigerator, not on counter. Re-crisp breading in an air fryer when possible.
Do not freeze fresh avocado, uncooked tomato/cucumber/cabbage salad, or mayonnaise/yogurt-based dressing unless kitchen-tested separately.
Freezer suitability here describes expected eating quality, not laboratory validated shelf life.
